title: Ayutthaya Historical Park
summary: Ayutthaya, founded around 1350 in central Thailand, was the Siamese capital until Burmese forces destroyed it in the 18th century. Its ruins, with prang towers and large monasteries, are preserved today as a historical park and World Heritage property.

uncertainty.note: The Fine Arts Department gives 1893 B.E., which is 1350 CE on the standard Buddhist Era offset (B.E. minus 543); UNESCO says founded c. 1350. Other chronicle-based accounts give 1351, so a small margin is allowed. End is the present: the ruins survive as a park.

as_recorded.value: established Krungsri Ayutthaya to be an administrative center in 1893 B.E.

when.display: Founded c. 1350 CE; destroyed 18th century; ruins preserved

where.modern_name: Ayutthaya Historical Park, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Thailand
where.historical_name: Krungsri Ayutthaya, capital of the Ayutthaya Kingdom (Siam)

importance.justification: Second capital of Siam after Sukhothai and the centre of a major trading kingdom; UNESCO-listed ruins.
